channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Conservation · Black Eyes Gallery
item.description: Black Eyes Gallery's second call asks a single question — what would you save? Conservation wants photographs of the land, buildings, species and traditions the photographer most wants still to be there in the future: cottonwoods on the U.S.–Mexico border that have stood two hundred years, acres of the Amazon already gone, plants and animals lost daily and mostly never photographed, buildings pulled down faster than anyone can record them, people threatened with destruction. The gallery's framing is that a photograph outlasts what it points at, and that the record is the one form of keeping available to almost anyone. Any genre is welcome so long as the work is photographic or lens based, and anything created entirely or substantially with artificial intelligence is disqualified. Twenty-five images are selected by juror Douglas Fur, a nationally exhibited Tucson photographer with a 2006 BFA from Cornish College of the Arts who spent two years at Decode Gallery and is now Artist Liaison and Gallery Manager for Tucson Erotica. Selected photographers send a file and nothing else: the gallery prints, mats and frames every accepted image at its own expense for the show at 485 S. Stone from 3 to 28 November 2026, then holds the single exhibition print in its archive for two years before destroying it. Accepted work also enters a permanent online archive carrying the artist's name, image title and social link, and is promoted across the gallery's social channels, email list and website with an individual feature on the Black Eyes Instagram. Entry is $40 for up to five images or $50 for up to ten; a reduced $20 fee is held for two artists per call on a first-come, first-served basis for anyone who writes in before submitting, and any entry that produces no selection earns $5 off the next one. Submissions are reviewed blind where possible, on creativity, originality, interpretation of the theme and how an image works against the exhibition as a whole, with CV and bio largely set aside. Work may optionally be offered for sale at a price the artist sets, the gallery retaining 50 per cent, and photographers keep full copyright throughout. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $50/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Solo & Small Group Exhibition Proposals · K Space Contemporary
item.description: K Space Contemporary is a 501(c)(3) non-profit in downtown Corpus Christi dedicated to presenting contemporary art in South Texas, and its exhibition committee reviews artist portfolios once a year to fill solo and small-group slots across four spaces — the Clower Gallery (29' x 22'), the Starr Gallery (50' x 30'), the Corner Spot (16' x 23') and the Project Space (11.5' x 14.5'). The annual application deadline is 1 February. All media are accepted, including site-specific and immersive installation, and applicants choose a gallery preference and an exhibition category of 2-dimensional, 3-dimensional, installation/immersive or mixed. The gallery is looking for original, innovative work not previously exhibited at K Space. There is no cost to apply, and submission is by digital portfolio only: an artist website or a link to a Google Drive or Dropbox folder set to "anyone with the link" so the committee can review it, plus a written exhibition proposal. Applicants must be 18 or older; entry is open to Texas artists, with particular interest in those living in the Texas Coastal Bend and South Texas. One application per artist per year is allowed. Submissions are accepted year round but reviewed only once, in spring, so an application filed shortly after a review waits ten to twelve months for an answer. Selected exhibitions are scheduled six to eighteen months in advance and run four to seven weeks; artists are responsible for delivering or shipping their own work and for installation and de-installation during gallery hours. K Space handles publicity — a press release to local and state media, an exhibition page on its site, an email invitation to around 2,000 subscribers, social promotion and 1,000 to 2,000 printed postcard announcements — and retains 40 per cent commission on gallery sales. Work must be collected or shipped out within ten days of the close; anything left 60 days after the last day becomes gallery property. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Athenaeum Solo or Group Show 2026–2027 · Northern Virginia Fine Arts Association
item.description: The Athenaeum Gallery, a Greek Revival landmark on Prince Street in Old Town Alexandria run by the Northern Virginia Fine Arts Association, sets aside part of its programme — an average of eight shows a year — for exhibitions proposed by artists and curators rather than chosen by the gallery director. This is the 2026–2027 review window, the successor to the cycle that closes on 30 September 2026: the portal opens the same day and accepts proposals through 30 September 2027, and the gallery describes the review as rolling rather than batched. Artists living or working in Virginia, Maryland or the District of Columbia may propose a solo show; a group of artists from the region may propose a group show; and a curator based anywhere may propose a show of work by artists from the area. Proposals are evaluated by gallery director Twig Murray on what the artist is trying to achieve or communicate, what makes the work distinctive, technical quality, and how recently the artist or the work has been shown locally. All visual media are welcome, photography included, but every work must be wall-mounted, less than nine inches deep and framed or fully finished, wired and ready to hang on picture hooks; nothing floor-mounted or free-standing is considered, and work requiring electricity is excluded. Sculpture may be entered only if it is under nine inches deep and lighter than 30 pounds. An application takes six to twelve images and up to three proposals per applicant are allowed. The artist, group or curator is responsible for getting work to the gallery and for collecting unsold work at the close. The Athenaeum insures everything in the show for the full retail price for the run, takes 40 per cent commission on sales and pays the artist within thirty days of closing; a curator-proposed show can negotiate a different split. Work does not have to be for sale to be included. Founded in 1964, the NVFAA is a registered 501(c)(3) supported by donations, member contributions, building rentals and sales commissions. — Deadline: September 30, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Inspired Annapolis · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County has given Maryland Federation of Art a show at the Annapolis Visitor's Center at 26 West Street in Historic Annapolis, a recently relaid space that around 800 people walk through every week, and MFA is filling it from this call. Entries must be inspired by or representative of Annapolis, Anne Arundel County or the 250th anniversary of the United States. Two-dimensional work only, in any medium, with no dimension exceeding 34 inches including edges and frame; photographic prints must have been analogue or digitally processed by the artist, who must have controlled cropping, colour balance, contrast and the final printing, and any limited-edition photographic print must be signed and numbered. Work made with image-generative AI is not accepted, and no reproductions are. All MFA exhibitions are blind juried, with artists' names and identifying information hidden from the juror; this one is selected by Jo Fleming, artist and director of Jo Fleming Contemporary Art, who took a BFA at MICA, grew up in the Appalachian mountains of Virginia and has shown abstract paintings about coal mining and global warming at the US Embassy in Ulaanbaatar and the American Institute in Taipei under the State Department's Art in Embassies exchange. Selected work hangs at the Visitor's Center from 2 November to 31 December 2026, with an in-person reception on 4 November; every entry meeting the criteria is considered. The juror's Best in Show award is a $70 one-year MFA membership. Entry is restricted to MFA member artists residing in any state or territory of the United States, Canada or Mexico, so a non-member must buy a membership — currently $70 a year — before entering; the entry fee itself is $15 for one or two works plus $5 for a third, and up to three original works made in the past three years may be entered. Artists are notified by 5 PM on 19 October and keep 70 per cent of sales, 75 per cent for members. Founded in 1963, MFA is a non-profit whose Circle Gallery in Annapolis is Maryland's oldest operating artist gallery. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: $15/2 works + $5 addl (members only). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: EYC Lights Parade Poster Competition 2026 · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Every year on the second Saturday of December the Annapolis harbour fills with boats strung with thousands of lights for the Eastport Yacht Club Lights Parade, and Maryland Federation of Art runs the competition that chooses the image the club uses to advertise it. Original two-dimensional work in any medium is welcome, and the brief is specific: the work must depict an Annapolis landmark or the Annapolis skyline, include one or more festively decorated boats, and incorporate the EYC burgee, a flag image downloadable from the entry page. Past winners are posted at eastportyc.org/lights-parade/artists. The winning piece is selected by a committee from Eastport Yacht Club, not by an MFA juror, and becomes the official image of the 2026 parade, reproduced on posters, note cards and other promotional material; EYC awards the chosen artist $2,500 and contributes up to $125 towards framing. Read the rights clause before entering: by submitting, an artist agrees that if their piece is chosen they grant EYC an irrevocable licence to use it and copies of it on various media in connection with promoting the Lights Parade — the clause as printed still names 2024 — and in future years, and are deemed to have gifted the original work to EYC, a 501(c)(7) organisation. Every entry is shown in MFA's Online Gallery from a reveal party in November through 31 December 2026, People's Choice voting closes at midnight on 16 December and the People's Choice winner, announced at 5 PM on 17 December, receives a $70 one-year MFA membership. Entry is open to all artists residing in any state or territory of the United States and costs $10 for one or two works; up to two original works made in the past three years may be entered, work previously shown in MFA's People's Choice Voting Gallery is not eligible, and work made with image-generative AI is not accepted. Because the winner's physical piece changes hands, size matters: the work may not be smaller than 24 inches in one direction by 30 inches in the other, and no dimension may exceed 36 inches including the frame. Artists keep 80 per cent of online sales, 85 per cent for MFA members, and MFA reimburses up to $40 of shipping on those sales for artists in the 48 contiguous states. The winner announcement date is listed only as TBA. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $10/2 works. Prize: $2,500.

item.title: Lowe House 2027 · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Maryland Federation of Art has been invited to hang a show in the Lowe House of Delegates Office Building at 6 Bladen Street in Annapolis, the working office building for the Maryland State Delegates, and this call fills it for a three-month run from 13 January to 12 April 2027 — a General Assembly session's worth of daily foot traffic from legislators, staff and visitors. Original two-dimensional work in any medium is eligible, with no dimension exceeding 30 inches in height or 24 inches in width including frame. Photographic prints must have been analogue or digitally processed by the artist, who must have controlled cropping, colour balance, contrast and the final printing, and any limited-edition photographic print must be signed and numbered; work made with image-generative AI is not accepted and no reproductions are. All MFA exhibitions are blind juried, with names and identifying information hidden from the juror. This edition is selected by Teddy Johnson, Academic Chair of Visual Arts and Associate Professor of Visual Arts at Anne Arundel Community College, where he was also Cade Gallery Director from 2017 to 2023; he holds a BFA from MICA and an MFA from the Lamar Dodd School of Art at the University of Georgia, has shown solo at the American Poetry Museum, the Bromo Seltzer Arts Tower and the Museum of the Shenandoah Valley, and has held residencies at La Macina di San Cresci in Chianti in each of the past four years. Awards designated by the juror total $500, presented at a virtual ceremony on Zoom on 20 January 2027. Entry is open to MFA members or to artists residing in Anne Arundel County, Maryland — everyone else needs a membership, currently $70 a year. The entry fee is $45 for one or two works, $30 for members, plus $6.75 each for up to four more ($4.50 for members), and up to six original works made in the past three years may be entered. Work previously exhibited at the Lowe House Office Building is not eligible for re-entry. Artists are notified at 5 PM on 10 December and keep 70 per cent of sales, 75 per cent for members. Founded in 1963, MFA is a non-profit whose Circle Gallery is Maryland's oldest operating artist gallery. — Deadline: November 11, 2026. Fee: $45/2 works ($30 members) + $6.75 each addl. Prize: $500 + exhibition.

item.title: In The City 2027 · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Skylines, crosswalks, alleyways and shops; bright lights, buses, taxis and crowds. Maryland Federation of Art's third In the City exhibition asks for work that carries the sense of an urban experience — the parts of city life that are universal and could be anywhere from a metropolis to a small town, and the symbols and iconic places that mark out one particular community, its restaurants, festivals, music halls and graffiti. Urbanite or visitor, the brief is a visual story of the city. Any original 2D or 3D work meeting MFA's guidelines is considered, with no dimension exceeding 72 inches including frame; artists may be asked to help install work over 60 inches or 40 pounds. Photographic prints must have been analogue or digitally processed by the artist, who must have controlled cropping, colour balance, contrast and the final printing, and any limited-edition photographic print must be signed and numbered; work made with image-generative AI is not accepted and no reproductions are. All MFA exhibitions are blind juried, with names and identifying information hidden from the juror. This edition is selected by Rob Pointon, a British painter who works primarily en plein air with an interest in wide-angle perspective and the depiction of movement; born in 1982, he took a first-class honours degree in fine art at Aberystwyth and studied at the Royal Drawing School in London, is a full member of the Royal Institute of Oil Painters and of the Manchester Academy of Fine Arts, and since 2021 has held residencies with the Household Cavalry and the wider Household Division. Awards designated by the juror total $1,000, presented at a virtual ceremony at 5:30 PM EST on 3 February 2027. Selected work hangs at MFA's Circle Gallery in Annapolis from 3 to 27 February 2027, with an in-person reception on the closing day. Entry is open to artists residing in any state or territory of the United States, Canada or Mexico and costs $45 for one or two works, $30 for MFA members, plus $6.75 each for up to four more ($4.50 for members); up to six original works made in the past three years may be entered, and work previously exhibited at Circle Gallery is not eligible for re-entry. Entry runs on ArtCall, where one "application" means one artwork; a second or third image of the same work may optionally be attached as a detail photograph. Artists are notified at 5 PM on 17 December and keep 70 per cent of sales, 75 per cent for members. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: $45/2 works ($30 members) + $6.75 each addl. Prize: $1,000 + exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Getxophoto Open Call
item.description: Getxophoto is an international image festival held in Getxo, on the Basque coast near Bilbao, since 2007, and is organised by the non-profit Begihandi Kultur Elkartea. Its programme is built almost entirely of open-air installations in public space, which the festival describes as a defence of physical and online public space as a place of meeting, experimentation and celebration; it also welcomes projects that emerge from online spaces and approach digitality critically. The 21st edition runs 27 May to 20 June 2027 under the theme "Tide", set by curator Cale Garrido, who asks for work that treats photography not as a static object but as a practice in constant movement - images that circulate, change context, are archived and retrieved - and for projects that make visible what had remained hidden, unsettle what seemed fixed, transform memory, or sketch new forms of collective action. Proposals may use photography, video, actions, installation, digital art or any other visual practice, and may be submitted in English or Spanish. Three winning artists each receive an exhibition or installation produced at the festival's cost, a €500 artist fee, two nights' accommodation during the Opening Week, travel support of up to €150 for international artists (€100 for national ones) and media coverage. An international jury decides by mutual agreement on artistic criteria, conceptual development and fit with the theme, with gender parity and inclusion also taken into account. Each project needs 10 to 20 images and costs €22 to submit; up to three projects may be entered, each at the same fee. Applicants from countries affected by war, or living in refugee camps, who cannot pay the fee are invited to write to the organisers about alternatives. The shortlist is announced on 26 November 2026 and results on 30 November. Copyright stays with the artist throughout; entries are not accepted by email. — Deadline: November 3, 2026. Fee: €22 per project. Prize: €500 + Exhibition.

item.title: Ploch Art Gallery 2027–2028 Season · Sharon Lynne Wilson Center for the Arts
item.description: The Sharon Lynne Wilson Center for the Arts is a multidisciplinary nonprofit arts facility in Brookfield, in the Greater Milwaukee area, and its Ploch Art Gallery gives Wisconsin visual artists a route to a solo or group show with roughly 87 linear feet of professionally lit wall space along the outer wall of the theatre balcony, open to the public and reached by stairs or lift. The annual call fills the 2027–2028 season, which runs 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028; exhibitions hang for one to two months and vary in length around the theatre schedule. Three kinds of proposal are accepted: an individual artist, a two-person, collaborative or existing artist group, and a curator proposing a themed show by several artists. Eligible media are enumerated as painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, photography, fibre arts, installation and mixed media; time-based media are not accepted and the work must be original, with no reproductions or giclée prints. Work must have been completed in the previous ten years, with a preference for newer and never-before-exhibited work, and because the centre hosts school groups it must be suitable for all ages. A vast majority of the work must be for sale and the centre takes a 30% consignment fee on any sale; exhibiting artists deliver, install and take down their own work, and nothing may be shipped. Selection for the 2027–2028 season is made by jurors Nina Ghanbarzadeh, a 2024 Mary L. Nohl Fellow in the Established Artist category, and Megan Woodard Johnson, a mixed-media artist and curator based in West Bend. Applicants must be 18 or older and must live in Wisconsin, be a native of Wisconsin, or hold a degree from a Wisconsin college or university; for a curated proposal at least half the exhibiting artists must meet that bar. An application takes 8–10 JPEGs, an image list, an artist statement, a bio of 250 words or less and a CV of up to two pages, with an optional 250-word exhibition proposal, and costs a non-refundable $20; two applications per artist are allowed. The application window is 1–31 October 2026 — the portal is not accepting entries before 1 October. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Untitled 2026 — A Photographic Exhibition · APA San Diego
item.description: Untitled is the annual juried competition and exhibition of APA San Diego, the Southwest regional chapter of American Photographic Artists, and the chapter describes it as open to anyone, from students to professional photographers, with no categories. There are no restrictions on genre or subject matter - portraiture, landscape, street, fine art, documentary, abstract and everything in between - and work may be titled or untitled. The 2026 jurors are Karen E. Haas, Lane Senior Curator of Photographs at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, where she looks after a collection of more than 6,000 prints spanning the history of western photography; Leah Ollman, who has written about art for more than 35 years for the Los Angeles Times, Art in America, Photograph, The Brooklyn Rail and ARTnews; and Amanda Smith, founder and co-director of A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas. The jurors select the top 30 images for an in-person exhibition, and the top three are awarded prizes; the organiser states those prizes go to photographers living in the U.S. The 2026 prize list gives Best in Show $500 cash, a ThinkTank FocusPoint Rolltop 30L, a full one-year Adobe Creative Cloud membership, a Nine Volt Powerbloc Flight and a George's Camera gift card; second place takes a ThinkTank FocusPoint Crossbody 13L with the Powerbloc and gift card, third place a ThinkTank Turnstyle 11L with the Powerbloc, gift card, a photography book library and a signed copy of Jason Lee's Galveston, and there is a People's Choice Award as well. A single image entry is one image and you may upload as many as you like, each charged at $10 for APA members or $20 for non-members; membership starts at $50 a year. Files must be JPG, no smaller than 1200 and at most 1800 pixels on the longest side, 72 ppi, sRGB, with no visible identifying text or symbols - entries are assigned an arbitrary ID for blind judging. No AI generative works are accepted. Entries close at 11:59 pm PST on October 13, 2026, and the chapter is donating 10% of entry fee proceeds to The WOO, a gallery and arts organisation in Barrio Logan working to expand affordable collaborative creative space for San Diego artists. — Deadline: October 13, 2026. Fee: $20 per image ($10 APA members). Prize: $500 cash + camera gear + Adobe Creative Cloud subscription + exhibition.

item.title: Face à la Mer x Magnum Learn Lab for Storytellers Scholarship
item.description: Magnum Photos and Face à la Mer are offering one fully funded place on the Magnum Learn Lab for Storytellers, Magnum's first long-term course: a ten-month international mentorship programme for twenty selected participants, built around immersive in-person residencies and sustained artistic and professional guidance, and supported by Magnum photographers Newsha Tavakolian, Antoine d'Agata and Rafał Milach alongside artist Tania Bohórquez and designer Ania Nalecka-Milach. The programme runs January to November 2027 in Italy, France and online. The scholarship goes to a photographer aged 18 or over living in North Africa - Magnum names Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Tunisia, Mauritania and Sudan - and covers the full course fee of $17,450 plus visa, travel and accommodation; the recipient must be able to cover their own expenses during the third on-site workshop, in Paris in November 2027. Applying is free and Magnum states plainly that applications "do not include any fees". The successful candidate is chosen during the rencontres photo de Tanger, Face à la mer, in Tangier on November 25-29 2026, after a 30-minute interview with Magnum photographer Antoine d'Agata, artist Tania Bohórquez, a representative of Magnum Photos and a representative of Face à la Mer; the applicant is notified on November 30 2026. Magnum is looking for photographers interested in documentary photography and in working on projects, who can demonstrate a strong ability to tell stories through photography, and it encourages applications from those underrepresented in the industry, including women and female-identifying photographers, people from lower socio-economic backgrounds, LGBTQIA+ photographers and those from ethnic minority backgrounds; no minimum formal qualification is required. Applications need one PDF holding one or two photo stories totalling no more than 30 images, plus a statement of purpose in English. Face à la Mer, the Tangier Photography Encounters, is co-founded and directed by artistic director Mina Mostefa and photojournalist Wilfrid Estève and describes itself as a professional event for contemporary photography in the Mediterranean, building a cultural bridge between Africa and Europe. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Full scholarship worth $17,450 plus visa, travel and accommodation.

item.title: Brian Tremain Bursary 2026 · Association for Historical and Fine Art Photography
item.description: The Association for Historical and Fine Art Photography (AHFAP) is accepting applications for the Brian Tremain Bursary, which funds attendance at its annual conference for photography students, recent graduates and early career professionals. Brian Tremain was one of AHFAP's founding members and his family has sponsored the bursary in his memory for several years; each award covers a conference ticket, costs towards travel and accommodation, and a year of free AHFAP membership. The association states that this will be the last year the bursary is awarded. AHFAP Conference 2026 runs 9-10 November at Stoller Hall in Manchester, and the association pitches the bursary as a chance to explore a career in cultural heritage photography, hear about imaging and digitisation projects, meet leading figures in the field and see demonstrations of current equipment; day two of the conference offers studio visits and workshops unique to the event. Applications go by email to Denise King at president@ahfap.org.uk and should be no more than one side of A4 in font 12, giving your name, contact details including address and phone number or the address of your business, institution or college, a short paragraph about yourself, a short paragraph about your institution or business and your position in it (or, if you are a student, the area of photography you are studying), and a short description of how receiving the bursary will help you in your work or studies. The judging panel is the association's Honorary President and its Chair; all entries are confidential, the judges' decision is final and no communication is shared about the decision-making process. The closing date is 30 September 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Conference fellowship + one year AHFAP membership.

item.title: FRESH EYES 2027
item.description: FRESH EYES is the worldwide open call run by Amsterdam-based GUP Magazine (Guide to Unique Photography), which has followed emerging photography talent since 2005 and has published its annual talent book since 2012. The 2027 edition invites emerging photographers from anywhere in the world to show their vision and expertise in their chosen photographic field, and the selected talents are presented in an atmospheric softcover publication. Each selected photographer gets a minimum of four pages in the book, three copies sent to them, international distribution to galleries, curators, magazines, newspapers and creative photo agencies, and promotion through the GUP and FRESH EYES channels. One image from each selected artist is displayed in a group presentation and book launch at the Haute Photographie Fair in Rotterdam in March 2027, with a free entrance ticket for the photographer and one guest, and portfolio reviews at the fair. Three exceptional talents are chosen by the curators as FRESH EYES Exceptional Talent Award winners and go into the book for free. A jury of GUP editors, gallerists and photographers reads the applications. Applying is free, but this is a pay-if-selected call and the numbers on the organiser's own site do not agree: the Info page says the rate for every selected participant is €350 excluding VAT and shipping, while the FAQ answers "what are the costs?" with €395 excluding VAT, asks "why should I pay €395?", and then answers that question with €350 - so budget for the higher figure. GUP states that it makes no profit from the fee and that it is invested in production, design and distribution of the books, the print exhibition and the launch event; shipping is extra if you cannot collect your copies at the launch. Submit a low-resolution portfolio of fifteen images with a brief artist statement; the FAQ sets a floor of ten images and asks for JPEGs between 500KB and 1MB each, up to 10MB in total. Only photographs are considered - pictures of installations, performances or books are not - and photographers previously selected must apply with a new body of work. Submissions close on October 21st. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: Free (€350–€395 participation fee if selected). Prize: Publication + exhibition at Haute Photographie Fair.

item.title: Graduate Artist Residency · OVADA
item.description: A free one-month studio residency at OVADA's warehouse on Osney Lane in central Oxford, running Friday 23 October to Thursday 19 November 2026. It is open to artists living in Oxfordshire who studied Fine Art - in Oxfordshire or elsewhere - and who graduated from university within the last 24 months; joint applications from two artists are welcome, and OVADA says it is particularly interested in practitioners who would benefit from dedicated studio space and a sustained period of time to develop their practice. The residency provides a central Oxford studio with 24-hour access, free Wi-Fi and power, communal facilities, a community of artists working in the studios, and a connection to the exhibitions and events programme across the warehouse; an open studio during the residency can be arranged with OVADA. Accommodation and materials are NOT provided, and the space must be fully vacated by 5:00pm on 19 November. Practical limits worth noting for process-based work: heavy machinery, welding tools and loud equipment are not permitted, and practices involving solvents, aerosols or materials requiring specialist ventilation cannot be undertaken indoors. Applicants submit a link to their website and/or artist Instagram, a PDF portfolio and a statement of up to 300 words on what they would like to gain from the residency, by Sunday 27 September at 12:00 PM. Two things to know before applying: the residency page names NO accepted media at all, so photography is neither named nor excluded - OVADA's own gallery open call that closed on 21 September did list photography among the media it welcomes - and although the page says an application form follows, no form or application link is published on it, so contact@ovada.org.uk is the only route OVADA gives. OVADA is a non-profit company limited by guarantee (no. 5138370). — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: One-month Oxford studio residency.

item.title: Jentel Artist Residency — Summer/Fall 2027
item.description: Residency at Jentel, a working cattle ranch 20 miles southeast of Sheridan in Banner, Wyoming, in the foothills of the Bighorn Mountains, for the Summer/Fall sessions running May 15 to December 7, 2027. Each residency is approximately three weeks long: residents arrive on the 15th of one month and leave on the morning of the 7th of the next, with six residents on site each session. Residents receive a private room, a shared living area and kitchen, a separate individual studio, and a $300 stipend distributed in weekly installments to help defray living and food costs; aside from the $30 application fee there are no additional charges to attend, though a $100 reservation deposit is due one month after notification and confirms participation. Residencies are intended as professional development for visual artists in any medium - photography included - as well as writers in fiction, creative nonfiction or poetry and composers across musical genres, and selections are made on artistic merit and promise by a rotating panel of visual art, literary and music professionals. Applicants must be 25 or over and must be US citizens or reside in the US during the year of the residency; artists in post-doc fellowships are eligible, but students enrolled full-time (9 hours or more) in a degree programme at the time of the session are not. Residents bring their own materials and laptops; pets are not allowed and accommodation for children or family members is not provided. Wyoming residents have a streamlined application. Note the application is not yet open: the portal goes live on October 1, 2026 and closes January 15, 2027 at 12:00 noon MST, with notification by March 15, 2027. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency + $300 stipend.

item.title: Artist Submissions · Carter Burden Gallery
item.description: Open, year-round submissions to Carter Burden Gallery, a Chelsea gallery at 548 West 28th Street devoted entirely to professional artists aged 60 and over. The gallery is a programme of the Carter Burden Network, a non-profit established in 1971 that promotes the well-being of seniors 60 and older, and it states its goal plainly: that older, lesser-known artists must not be overlooked due to age or decreased marketability in the current art scene. It focuses on NYC artists over 60 and describes its community as re-emerging professional artists, exhibiting work it calls vibrant, cutting-edge and important regardless of the artist's age. Submissions are accepted from professional older artists, aged 60 and older, currently living and working in the New York City metropolitan area full time, working in any medium - photography included - who are interested in exhibiting their work. There is no fee and no deadline: applicants email submissions@carterburdennetwork.org with either a link to their website or 10-20 JPEGs representative of recent work (72dpi, no larger than 400-500kb), the date, medium, dimensions and pricing of all works, and a CV and bio, and must state the area they are based in and their age in the body of the email. The gallery reviews submissions three times a year, and it recommends visiting the gallery before submitting. It does not accept mail-in submissions or walk-in portfolio reviews. Separately from this rolling route, Carter Burden also runs nationally open juried exhibitions on its own schedule. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Gallery exhibition.

item.title: Visual Artist AIRspace Residency 2027–2028 · Abrons Arts Center
item.description: Abrons Arts Center, the arts programme of Henry Street Settlement on New York's Lower East Side, supports a cohort of three early-career visual artists across a 20-month residency that begins January 5, 2027 and runs to August 2028 — the Submittable prospectus defines Year 1 as January to August 2027 and Year 2 as September 2027 to August 2028, with the closing group exhibition opening in spring 2028. Each resident gets a semi-private studio at Abrons for the full 20 months, an annual honorarium of $7,000, an annual materials stipend of $5,000, 30 hours of fully subsidised time in the centre's dance studios, studio visits with curators and arts professionals, professional development with the Arts Education department, paid opportunities to share work in progress through public programming, and a group exhibition at Abrons at the end of the residency. Every resident is paired with a professional artist mentor who is an alum of the programme, meeting one to one each month; the 2027–2028 mentors are Park McArthur (AIRspace 2013–14), Baseera Khan (2016–17) and Elliott Jerome Brown Jr. (2019–20), a Brooklyn-based artist and photographer whose own practice uses photography to explore representation through privacy and fiction. The call is for visual artists and names no medium list, but photographers are visibly part of the programme's lineage through Brown and past fellows. Applicants must be based in New York City and living within the five boroughs both at the time of application and during the residency, must not be in a degree-granting programme or a student during the residency period, and must fit Abrons' own definition of early career — actively making and sharing original work but without many opportunities yet to exhibit, take up residencies or grow professionally, with age and years of practice explicitly not factors. Applications are free, made through Submittable, and close October 4, 2026 at 11:59pm ET; the residency page adds that the call also closes early if 200 applications are reached. Review runs to November 2, in-person interviews are November 16–20, and invitations go out in December 2026. Funded by the Jacques and Natasha Gelman Foundation. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $7,000/year honorarium + $5,000/year materials stipend + studio + group exhibition.

item.title: Phoebe Journal Issue 56.1 — Visual Art
item.description: Phoebe is a journal of literature and art published at George Mason University since 1971, printing one winter print issue and one spring contest issue each year. This is the visual art call for the winter 2027 print issue, 56.1, open from August 15 to October 15, 2026 for both the cover image and the interior print and online gallery. Phoebe pays: $30 per accepted piece of visual art plus a copy of the issue, and work chosen for the print issue is also featured on the magazine's website. The editors ask for one to five high-resolution images as .png, .tif or high-quality .jpeg at 300 dpi or more and at least 1 MB, with PDFs acceptable for multiple works; the brief is simply quality art from artists at any stage of their career, with an eye for work that illustrates a narrative or conveys an emotion. Phoebe does not enumerate accepted media, but photography is plainly in the mix — the journal's own Visual Art archive for the current issue includes Leah Oates' 'Transitory Space', described as colour photography shot with an analogue camera on 35mm film, alongside Robert Frede Kenter's digital photo collage. Previously published work is not considered; simultaneous submissions are encouraged provided you withdraw promptly. AI-generated writing and artwork are not accepted, though digital manipulation and digital art are welcome. Phoebe retains first North American serial rights and all other rights remain the artist's, reverting immediately on publication. The submission fee is $3 in all genres including visual art, and fee waivers can be requested by email for artists for whom that is a hardship; the journal explicitly welcomes BIPOC, LGBTQ+ and international artists. Current and former students of George Mason's creative writing programme and other GMU affiliates are not eligible. Responses are aimed at 30 days after the submission period closes. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $3. Prize: $30 per piece + Publication (print).

item.title: Sixi International Artist-in-Residence Project 2027
item.description: Sixi Museum is a non-profit institution in Nanjing combining collection, exhibition, academic research and public education, and its International Artist-in-Residence Project, launched in 2024, is recruiting for three-month residencies in two 2027 sessions — spring, March to May, and autumn, September to November, with the exact dates set around the selected artists' preferences; the programme describes itself as “capable of accommodating two artists concurrently”. The project runs on a non-profit basis and covers the visa application, round-trip flights, insurance for the stay, accommodation in either a private apartment in the city centre or a private loft studio on the outskirts, personnel and technical assistance, and a material allowance; support also includes airport pickup, a welcome packet, orientation, English–Mandarin translation, project liaison and introductions to the local art scene. Residents take part in artist talks, workshops and open studios during the stay, Sixi expects a tangible and presentable outcome, and residents have the opportunity to show that work in an exhibition at the end; the artist is also expected to donate a selection of the work made during the residency to Sixi Museum. The 2027 call has two themes and an application may address either: 'Flux and Imprints: Contemporary Echoes of Migration History', on cross-regional mobility, cultural reconstruction and memory — the family histories of overseas Chinese, the legacy of colonialism in Asia, identity within global geopolitical frameworks, and the tension between archives, oral history and personal memory; and 'Folds of Text: Cross-Media Intertextuality and Intervention', which treats text as a fluid medium and invites interdisciplinary work across literature, linguistics, music and sound, and the visual arts. Artists from all disciplines are welcome and the call names no media list, but the programme's own record includes photographers — the 2025 winter resident Oscar Lebeck is described by the museum as a German artist who moves between photography in his study of the structural remains of cultural sites. Applicants must be at least 18 and able to complete the whole residency, there is no nationality restriction, and sufficient spoken and written Mandarin or English is required. Applications go by email to Sixi as a single PDF or ZIP containing a CV with profile photo, an artist portfolio and a residency proposal, with 'Residency Application' in the subject line; international applicants are told to allow two to three months for visa processing. The Sixi AiR Committee assesses the documents, may hold a video interview, and promises a final response no later than mid-February 2027. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded 3-month residency + accommodation + travel and materials budget.

item.title: MacDowell Fellowship — Fall 2027/Winter 2028
item.description: MacDowell's Fall/Winter 2027–2028 cycle, for residencies running September 1, 2027 to February 29, 2028 at the 450-acre estate in Peterborough, New Hampshire. A Fellowship consists of exclusive use of a private studio, accommodations and three prepared meals a day for two to eight weeks; artists may request up to eight weeks and the average stay is 30 days, with no minimum length. There are no residency fees, and Fellows may afterwards apply for need-based stipends and travel reimbursement grants. About 300 artists in seven disciplines are awarded Fellowships each year and MacDowell states the sole criterion for acceptance is artistic excellence. Photographers apply under Visual Arts, which MacDowell describes as considering makers of three-dimensional and two-dimensional art 'from photographers and printmakers to sculptors and creators of large-scale installation as well as everything in between'; the campus photography studio houses a private black-and-white analogue darkroom, but MacDowell does not provide digital photography equipment and chemicals and paper must be supplied by the artist. Applications are welcomed from artists of all backgrounds and all countries and from artists at any stage of practice, but applicants cannot be enrolled in a degree-seeking programme during the residency season they are applying for — doctoral candidates who have completed all coursework may apply — and artists may submit only one application every 24 months. Visual Arts applicants submit eight examples of work completed within the last four years. The reference-letter requirement remains suspended. Note the application is not yet open: it goes live on January 15, 2027 at macdowell.org/apply/apply-for-fellowship and closes February 10, 2027. A nonrefundable $30 processing fee is charged with each application, payable by card in the online form, with waivers available on request for significant financial hardship or where economic sanctions prevent payment; waiver requests are only considered from the opening of the application to three business days before the deadline. Applicants are notified roughly 2.5 months after the deadline, at the end of April. — Deadline: February 10, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Funded residency of two to eight weeks.

item.title: Los Fotógrafos 2027 · OBRA Collective
item.description: The fifth annual Los Fotógrafos exhibition at OBRA Collective Gallery in Charlotte, North Carolina — a photography-only group show for Latine/o/a/x photographers with ties to Latin America and Iberia. OBRA (Observe, Bridge, Respond, Art) is an interdisciplinary Latinx arts group founded in 2013 out of the Latin American Coalition and now a 501(c)(3) running classes, workshops, artist studios and a gallery on the ground floor of Charlotte's VAPA Center. The call is free to enter and open to Latine photographers based in Charlotte and the surrounding area, with original work in all styles of photography; AI-generated images are disqualified. One to ten pieces may be submitted, and the gallery will tell selected photographers how many of their pieces it can hang, with a 20-inch cap on width; the gallery takes a 20% commission, so price accordingly. Work must be delivered in person — the exhibition opens Saturday, January 9 and closes Saturday, February 6, 2027, and decisions go out by Monday, November 9, 2026. Two things to know before you apply. The organiser's Spanish text contradicts its English text in two places: it calls this the second annual rather than the fifth, and it dates artwork delivery to November 11-13 where the English says December 11-13, so confirm the drop-off window with the gallery. And OBRA's own website does not carry this call — its exhibitions page still shows 2024 shows — so the EntryThingy listing and the gallery's Instagram are where the current edition lives. The 2025 edition, themed Right Now, was covered by Enlace Latino NC and selected ten photographers; the organiser contact is photographer and community activist Héctor Vaca Cruz. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Enchanted Winter · Mountain Artists Guild
item.description: The Mountain Artists Guild's holiday juried show in Prescott, Arizona, on the theme of wintertime — snow-covered landscapes and quiet winter nights, frosted forests, glowing lights, winter wildlife, celestial skies, folklore and whimsical winter worlds, with the Guild explicitly saying work need not be Christmas-themed and that abstract readings of frost, ice and snowfall are welcome. Photography is one of the four judged categories in its own right ("all types of photography mediums"), alongside original paintings, three-dimensional objects and handcrafted jewellery, and the Guild's own media list names photography twice. Awards are placings rather than cash: Best of Show across all four categories, then 1st, 2nd and 3rd Place within Photography, plus honourable mentions. The call is open to members and non-members alike, with Arizona artists particularly encouraged; up to five works may be entered, the first three covered by the base fee and each further work charged separately ($10 members, $12 non-members). Accepted work also stays in the Guild's online Web Gallery for three months after the awards. Two practical bars: all artwork must be delivered in person on intake day, October 26, with no shipping permitted at all — only members who cannot make intake may ask the Gallery Manager to arrange something else, and every piece must be for sale, priced to absorb the Guild's commission (25% members, 40% non-members). Framed or gallery-wrapped work only, minimum 154 square inches and maximum 1,728 square inches including frame. The show runs October 28 to December 30, 2026; the juror had not been named when this was listed. — Deadline: October 17, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $45 non-members (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art Crit Night — November 2026 · Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition
item.description: A free, curator-led public critique run by the Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition, the statewide service organisation for Oklahoma artists. Two Oklahoma visual artists are selected per edition to present their work in person at 1515 Lincoln Gallery in Oklahoma City, receive structured feedback from the guest curator, and take questions from an audience of artists, arts professionals and collectors. Selected artists receive a $100 stipend and the application is free. The November 12, 2026 edition is led by Alexa Goetzinger, an independent curator, grant writer and development consultant based in Oklahoma City, who curated ArtNow: Materials and Boundaries at Oklahoma Contemporary in 2026, co-curated the national print exchange Connect: Collect and its exhibition Print as Object for Oklahoma City University's Hulsey Gallery from 2019 to 2023, and was previously Associate Director of OVAC itself. Work is shown to the room by projector, so documentation quality matters and detail shots help; smaller physical works can sometimes be accommodated, performance must be submitted as video, and artists may ask for the critique to focus on a website, an artist statement or a residency application instead of a body of work. The application asks for an artist statement, a bio, a stated goal for the critique and artwork samples. No medium is enumerated — the call says only "Oklahoma visual artists" and nothing excludes photography, whose projected presentation the format suits; OVAC's Grants for Artists programme has funded photographers, but this programme publishes no roster that affirms it. Applications close October 11 and artists are notified October 20. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $100.

item.title: Small Art Show 2026 · Paseo Arts Association
item.description: The Paseo Arts Association's annual small-works juried exhibition, held in Gallery II of the Paseo Arts & Creativity Center in Oklahoma City's historic Paseo Arts District through November and December. The brief is deliberately collector-friendly: original work no larger than 15 inches in any direction including frame, priced between $25 and $199. Open to all mediums of visual art in two and three dimensions, and the PAA's own preparation guidance names photography directly — "photos printed on metal do not need wire, if the hanging hardware is provided" — while the association also runs a dedicated annual photography show, Paseo Photofest, and a photography studio at the PACC. Reproduction prints are not eligible. Awards are cash: one Best of Show at $150, two Merit Awards at $75 each, and four to six honourable mentions, announced by the juror at the opening reception during the Paseo Arts District's First Friday Gallery Walk on November 6. The 2026 juror is Erica Nkechi, Executive Director of Heart Studios. The flat fee covers up to three works and is $15 for PAA members, $20 for everyone else; membership starts at $40 a year. Two things to plan for: artwork must be dropped off in person in Oklahoma City on Saturday, October 31 and collected on Saturday, December 19, and all work must be for sale. The association's commission on this show is stated inconsistently on its own site — the entry form and the call page both say 30%, while the juried-shows overview page says 30% generally but 20% for the Small Art Show — so confirm the rate before pricing. Entries close October 5 and selections are announced October 10. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: $15 members / $20 non-members (up to 3 works). Prize: $150.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — February 2027 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online. Dek Unu Magazine publishes and promotes fine art photography exclusively, and all fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview, and there is no word limit on the artist's own account of the work. The jurors read the documents as well as the images, and the magazine says it looks for coherent, intentional art, straight to strange, alongside technical excellence. The submission window for the February issue runs December 1-20, 2026, with the magazine closed for jury from the 21st to the 1st of the following month; submissions are by a single email carrying 11 separately named images plus bio and project commentary, with no zips, Dropbox or shared folders accepted. Entrants must be at least 18, and submission is limited to artists not previously published by Dek Unu. Dek Unu charges no fee to submit and does not pay contributors; copyright in the images always remains with the artist, and the magazine takes only the right to publish and to promote the magazine and the artist. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Art + Science Competition 2026: States of Change · Lenscratch
item.description: Lenscratch's annual Art + Science Award, now in its 2026 edition under the theme States of Change. The brief asks for photography that examines transition, transformation and instability within lived experience — change that may be gradual or abrupt, visible or difficult to perceive, ranging from emotional shifts to environmental conditions — and invites artists to consider how photography can reveal states where boundaries are not fixed and conditions keep shifting. Lenscratch's own submissions page frames the wider competition as looking for new work made within the last five years that shows an intersection of art and science, with topics as broad as climate change, environmental challenges or artificial intelligence. Awards are $500 for first place, $300 for second and $200 for third, plus two honourable mentions. The jurors are Linda Alterwitz, the Las Vegas interdisciplinary artist whose work integrates scientific inquiry with photographic processes and whose project Injection Site showed at FORMAT in Derby, and Ben Hickey, Executive Director of the Center for Exploratory and Perceptual Arts in Buffalo and previously curator of exhibitions at the Hilliard Art Museum. Entry is via a Google Form; Lenscratch states no entry fee on either of its two pages for this award, and every Lenscratch call in this directory is free. Winners are published on Lenscratch, which has run a daily photographer feature since 2007 and carries an archive of past Art and Science winners. The deadline is October 9, 2026. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 + $300 + $200.

item.title: 2027 Lighthouse Works Fellowship
item.description: A six-week fellowship on Fishers Island, New York, from an organisation devoted both to developing artists and to the year-round cultural life of the island. Fellows get a private bedroom in a three-storey Victorian house shared with the other fellows, all meals — Lighthouse Works staff cook and eat dinner with fellows most nights, and all dietary needs are accommodated — a private studio about a mile and a half from the house, flooded with light and facing the ocean, and $1,750 in stipends. There is a wood and metal fabrication shop and a kiln on site. The primary obligation is simply to pursue your work; the only two commitments are an Artist Talk and an Open Studio, which bookend the stay. The organisation runs three fellowship tracks — Visual Art, Fiction and Composer — and states that artists at any stage of their career are encouraged to apply, with artistic excellence the primary criterion for acceptance. It publishes no list of accepted media, so a photographer applies under Visual Art, but its own roster of past fellows settles the question: Genesis Baez, whose photographs the Museum of Modern Art has collected, Peng Ke, a RISD photography graduate and Magnum Foundation fellow, and Widline Cadet and Lachell Workman, both photography graduates, have all held fellowships here. Applicants must be at least 21 and must not be currently enrolled in a BFA or MFA programme; Lighthouse Works primarily considers US-based artists, though international artists with a demonstrated history of living and working in the United States are also invited, and collaboratives, duos and collectives are not accepted this cycle. Applications for the 2027 cycle are open September 1 to October 1, 2026 (11:59pm ET) through SlideRoom, with a $25 application fee — a limited number of waivers are granted first come, first served if you email before you submit. The visual-art work sample is up to ten files, and only the first five are read in the opening round. Selection panels — a jury of experts in each applicant's field — meet from mid-October through December, interviews are scheduled in early January and results go out in mid-January. The 2027 calendar runs five sessions between March 9 and November 30, 2027. This year's programme is supported in part by a grant from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $25 (waivers available). Prize: $1,750 stipend + six-week residency.

item.title: 2027 Wildacres Residency
item.description: A one-week residency in a private cabin on a mountain in Little Switzerland, North Carolina, offered at no cost to the artist. Wildacres has run the programme since 1999 and hosts around seventy artists a year in three self-catering cabins a quarter-mile beyond the retreat entrance, in weekly sessions running Monday afternoon to Sunday morning from April through October. One cabin is fully ADA compliant; another has a loft so two people collaborating on a single project can apply together. There is no internet in the cabins and cellphones generally do not connect except in the main retreat building — the isolation is the point. Residents may eat in the dining room with other residents, guests and staff, or cook for themselves. A few two-week residencies are offered each year, applied for separately on the form and not guaranteed. Artists cover their own travel and supplies; partners, guests and pets are not permitted, since these are working retreats. The selection committee is made up of artists, writers, musicians, actors, scholars and former residents, who review applications by discipline, and the programme is open to all artistic disciplines. The application form's discipline picker is organised by form rather than medium — Writing (fiction, non-fiction, poetry, memoir), Visual Arts three-dimensional, Visual Arts two-dimensional, Performance Arts music and dance, and Other — so a photographer applies as two-dimensional visual arts; work samples are no more than ten images. Applications for the 2027 calendar year opened August 1 and close at midnight EST on October 15, 2026, with a $30 non-refundable processing fee paid separately by PayPal after the form is submitted. Past residents must wait two years before reapplying. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: One-week residency.

item.title: Grants for Artists · Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition
item.description: The Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition's standing grant programme for individual Oklahoma artists, free to apply and reviewed on a rolling schedule with the next deadline on October 15, 2026. Four grants run under one umbrella. Creative Projects awards up to $1,500 to help an artist make visual art for public presentation. Community/Artist Partnership awards up to $1,500 for artist-led community projects. Education Assistance awards up to $500 toward training and professional development. Professional Basics awards up to $500 toward the ordinary infrastructure of a practice. Creative Projects and Community/Artist Partnership are reviewed twice a year, in March and October; Education Assistance and Professional Basics three times, in January, March and October. The grants are open to artists working in visual-based mediums as well as to curators and art writers, and OVAC publishes a scoring matrix and a sample application for each category, so you can see exactly what a panel is looking at before you write. It also gives written feedback on every request, funded or not. Photographers are among the funded: three of the March 2026 grantees work in photography — Liz Cousins, a Tulsa portrait photographer, for Queer Tulsa; Nicol Ragland for The Legends of Black Rodeo; and Barbara Paradise Kelly for matting, framing and display pedestals. Applicants must be 21 or over and must have lived in Oklahoma for at least the twelve months before the deadline; artists currently enrolled in BFA or MFA programmes are not eligible, and you may attach your name to only one application per cycle. You do not need to be an OVAC member. Funded projects must happen after the award and within a year of receiving the funds. Expect notification within four weeks of the deadline. Applications go through Submittable. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $1,500.

item.title: The Meridian Award 2026 — Cycle II
item.description: An independent international award granting a $1,000 fully unrestricted cash prize to one contemporary artist working in any medium, founded in New York City and open to artists worldwide aged 18 and over, with no restriction on nationality, location, education or professional status. There is no theme; portfolios are judged on artistic merit, clarity of vision, coherence of the work presented and the strength of a distinct artistic perspective. Photography is named in the award's own discipline list alongside painting, drawing, digital art, sculpture, print-based media, textile-based media, performance, sound art, video art and interdisciplinary practice; short and feature-length films are the only stated exclusion. Each cycle selects one winner and two finalists, and all three are invited to record an online interview published on the award's website and Instagram — but only the winner receives the $1,000. Apply through the award's own site with a short bio, an artist statement, a work description and up to five files, images and video links combined, with a $25 non-refundable fee; a discounted early-bird rate opens each cycle and fee waivers are not offered. Collaborative teams may apply as one. Artists keep full copyright, and the award takes only promotional reproduction rights on selected work. One thing to weigh: the jurors are described as invited contemporary-art professionals but are not publicly named. The inaugural 2026 cycle went to Brooklyn sculptor Wen Liu, a 2026 AIM Fellow at the Bronx Museum with fellowships from Yaddo, MacDowell and Bogliasco, with painter Matt Bollinger and interdisciplinary artist Andrius Alvarez-Backus as finalists. Cycle II closes October 15, 2026 and the winner is announced in mid-November. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: see-zeen Issue 21 Open Call
item.description: The twenty-first issue of an independent online photography magazine run out of New York and Berlin, open to any kind of photographic expression — portrait, landscape, documentary, fashion, abstract and anything else — with no theme set and no entry fee. Anyone over 18, anywhere in the world, may submit a series of six to fifteen images; the magazine asks for a project statement of up to 300 words, a work description of up to 100 words, a short bio with an email address, and website and Instagram links if you have them. Images go in as single JPG files, 2500 pixels maximum on the longest side, 72dpi in sRGB, each filename carrying the photographer's name and project title. Images and text files go together into a Dropbox file request; the magazine asks you to press Upload in Dropbox and then Send on the form at see-zeen.com. Copyright always remains with the photographer; by submitting you agree that see-zeen may publish and distribute the images on its website, social media and other media in connection with its own brand, and that the editors may crop images and make curatorial decisions. Everything submitted is also considered for the magazine's Instagram. The editors say plainly that they are overwhelmed with submissions and cannot contact photographers whose work is not selected, so there is no notification date. The Issue 21 deadline is October 18, 2026. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Women United Art Magazine — Issue XV
item.description: The Autumn 2026 issue of an international quarterly print and digital magazine dedicated to women in the arts, distributed worldwide through Amazon. The call is open to all women artists regardless of age, experience, education, race, sexual orientation or location, and the magazine states its focus explicitly: painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, digital art, collage, fibre and textile art, sculpture and installation. Selected artists are featured in Issue XV in either the In The Spotlight or The Curator's Pick section — the editors decide the length — plus a social media feature and a complimentary digital copy; artists picked for In The Spotlight are contacted with further questions about their work and practice. Everyone who submits receives a complimentary digital copy, and artists not selected for this issue may submit to the following one free of charge. The entry fee is a self-assessed sliding scale with no proof asked for: €35 standard for artists with stable income, institutional support or grant funding, €25 reduced for early-career or freelance artists, the underemployed and those carrying unpaid care responsibilities, and €10 symbolic for students and artists facing economic or structural limitations. The magazine says the fees fund waivers for artists who need them. Prepare an artist bio and an artist statement of up to 300 words each and between two and four images at a minimum of 300 DPI, cropped and ready for print, each filename formatted NAME_TITLE_YEAR_DIMENSIONS_MEDIA. Entries close 15 October 2026, selected artists are announced 25 October 2026 and the issue publishes in late November 2026. Editor-in-Chief is Mona Lerch, who founded Women United ART MOVEMENT in 2021. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: €10–€35. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Deep Shadows: The 2026 Lenscratch Halloween Exhibition
item.description: Lenscratch's Halloween show — the site has been running one on and off since 2011 — a free online juried exhibition for images that step out of the everyday and into the uncanny. The site's framing is that Halloween and photography go together in their shared ability to suspend reality and put the strange centre stage, and it asks for one picture that interprets the magic and suspense of the season. Juror Douglas Breault will select fifty images for the exhibition. Entry is free and strictly one image per photographer, submitted through a Google Form with a caption formatted exactly as Lenscratch specifies — copyright symbol, your name, title, location, website, Instagram handle. Submissions close October 18, 2026. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Belgrade Photo Month — New Talents 2027
item.description: The ninth edition of the Belgrade Photo Month festival opens its New Talents call to a younger generation of photographers, free to enter and open to any nationality, professional or amateur, on one hard condition: you must have been born after 1 January 2002. The theme is REBORN — to be reborn is to enter a new state, suggesting change but also continuity — and the festival explicitly leaves the reading open, welcoming any photographic genre or artistic approach that works through people, places, memories, identities, communities, nature or society. Entries are one project of eight to fifteen photographs, titled and numbered in viewing order, at a maximum 1920 pixels on the long side, sent by email with an artist's statement, a short CV including your birth date, and a text about the proposal of no more than 3,000 characters in English. AI photographs are not accepted. Proposals submitted to previous editions cannot be resubmitted. The jury — Joan Alvado, Julio Pantoja, Shirin Abedi, Sigrid Debusschere and Vesna Latinović — picks three best proposals plus the best local Serbian proposal, then awards first, second and third place and a prize for the best local proposal; all four projects are shown in the New Talents 2027 exhibition during the festival in Belgrade. The festival does not publish what the prizes consist of. Copyright and all other author's rights stay with the photographer, who is credited in every official festival publication and in the exhibition; nominated and winning photographs join the Belgrade Photo Month collection, and entrants accept that the organisers and general sponsors may use submitted photographs to promote the festival. Submissions close 14 February 2027 at 23:30 Belgrade time, successful authors are notified 7 March 2027 and the exhibition opens 7 May 2027. — Deadline: February 14, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Ephemeral Beauty — 2027 Juried Art Exhibition · Kahilu Theatre
item.description: The annual juried exhibition of Kahilu Exhibits, the visual arts programme of Kahilu Theatre in Waimea on Hawaiʻi Island, built this cycle around flowers and the paradox that the most fleeting thing in nature is also the one most permanently woven into human civilisation. The guest juror is Andrzej Kramarz, Gallery Director of the East Hawaiʻi Cultural Center in Hilo, and the brief ranges deliberately wide — flowers as signals of fertile land and water, as the lotus of Buddhist thought, as the blood-born blooms of Greek myth, as the ʻōhiʻa and lehua of Hawaiian moʻolelo — inviting artists to work anywhere in that territory. No medium list is published for this show; the brief's own note on what is sought says all approaches are welcome and asks artists to respond to the flower “across any medium”, and Kahilu Exhibits' separate call for exhibition proposals names photography among the media it programmes. Open internationally to artists 18 and over. The fee is $25 for the first sample and $5 for each additional media sample; accepted work hangs in Kahilu's Simperman and Suli T. Go Galleries with an opening reception on Thursday, January 14, 2027, and artists pay shipping both ways (Kahilu asks for two-day shipping or Mokulele Airlines' Wikiwiki service to Waimea-Kohala Airport, and specifically not ground services). Sales split 60% to the artist, 40% to Kahilu, and Kahilu retains sales rights for 45 days after the exhibition closes; work does not have to be offered for sale. One caution worth knowing before you apply: the listing's own prose is part-recycled from the previous cycle — it calls the show the "2026 Juried Art Exhibition", gives an impossible run of "January 14, 2026 through February 28, 2027", and dates the submission deadline "Friday, December 12, 2025" with notifications "Monday, December 22, 2025", while the platform's machine deadline field, last edited 14 September 2026, closes entries on 7 December 2026. The 2027 dates in the shipping and reception block are all weekday-correct, the 2025 ones are weekday-correct for 2025, so the stale block is the December one. Apply by 7 December to be safe, and confirm with the gallery if you need the later date. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: $25 + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: WHEN NATURE CALLS: A Call for Nature Art · The Lab on Santa Fe
item.description: A selected group show at The Lab on Santa Fe, a gallery in Denver's Art District on Santa Fe with strong First Friday traffic, asking for nature work that looks past the postcard. The brief is unusually well written and unusually broad: landscapes, wildlife, plants, weather, water, geology, the human body in nature and the many ways we live with, depend on, alter and imagine the natural world, with observation and invention equally welcome. Nature here can be majestic or microscopic, peaceful or vicious, funny, sacred, invasive, decaying, returning or completely indifferent to us; the gallery says it is especially drawn to the things most people walk right past. All styles and mediums are welcome, from traditional landscape, botanical study and wildlife art to abstraction, surrealism, conceptual work and full experimentation. The gallery publishes no list of eligible or excluded media beyond that line, and nowhere calls the show juried or names a selector — it says only that acceptance is not guaranteed and that reviewing art costs it significant time and money — but it has run a dedicated international street photography exhibition in this same space, so lens-based work is in scope. Location eligibility is listed as national rather than Colorado-only, one or two works per artist, $34 to enter. All submitted work must be for sale and the split on sales is 58% to the artist, 42% to the gallery; the gallery states plainly that acceptance is not guaranteed and that fees are non-refundable. The exhibition runs April 2 to May 1, 2027. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $34. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 3rd Annual Printmaking Micro-Residency · The Cedars Union
item.description: A month-long printmaking micro-residency at The Cedars Union, a non-profit artist incubator in Dallas, free to apply and open to artists of any medium — the call says so explicitly, and adds that no prior printmaking experience is required. One artist is selected to work with Taylor Gibson, the organisation's manager of programming, to brainstorm, produce and curate a closed edition of twenty hand-pulled prints in the process of their choosing: relief, intaglio, screenprint or collagraph. The imagery and every technical decision — number of layers, colours, composition, paper, image size, embellishments — are the artist's, all materials are provided, and ownership of the image stays with the artist, with The Cedars Union retaining the right to use it for marketing and outreach. The edition becomes a thank-you gift for the organisation's major donors. The artist receives a $400 stipend, five prints from the finished edition and a print placed in The Cedars Union's permanent collection. Apply with a 200-word proposal for what you intend to produce and how your work would translate into printmaking, optionally with sketches, plus three to five examples of relevant work. Two conditions to weigh before applying: you must be a current Cedars Union member (Community or Cohort) both when you apply and during the residency, and Community Membership is $80 a month on a six-month commitment or $100 month to month, so the residency is realistically for artists already in or moving to Dallas; and you agree to be present for the entire project. Community Membership applications are accepted year round. Previous recipients were Victoria Brill and Bao Nghi Ngo. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $400 stipend.

item.title: You'll Covet Your Eye Out — Holiday Show · Covet Art Gallery
item.description: A holiday group exhibition at Covet Art Gallery, a storefront at 1922-A South Coast Highway in Oceanside, north of San Diego, open since 2023, built around a single constraint: every work must be priced at $500 or less. Size is explicitly irrelevant — a tiny treasure and a statement piece compete on the same terms — and the gallery is after work that is covetable, collectible and giftable, whether someone is buying for a person they love or for themselves. All mediums and styles are welcome, all career levels, and the call is open nationally and internationally. Work must be original and must be for sale; the sale price given at entry is final and sales split 50/50 with the gallery, while artists are also invited to list further work on the gallery's own online marketplace, where the split is 70% to the artist. Artists retain full copyright and cover delivery both ways. Entry is $25 plus $5 for each additional image, up to twenty images. The show runs November 7 to December 12, 2026, with an opening party on November 7 from 5 to 9pm and a closing party on December 12. There is no cash award and no juror is named, though the gallery's own artist agreement calls this a Juried Group Exhibition — what is on offer is a selected place on the wall of a real gallery over the selling season. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $25 + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Non-Verbal Co-Learning Engagement — Spring 2027 · grunt gallery
item.description: A six-week paid engagement at grunt gallery in Vancouver for artists whose practice runs on gesture, text, signed languages or silence rather than speech. Two artists are selected and each receives $2,000 CAD, spendable entirely at their own discretion with no reporting to grunt; no completed artwork is required and no materials or artwork have to be handed over. The commitment is up to eight hours of co-learning: six weekly silent check-ins online, one interpreted or hybrid staff meeting, one silent accessibility committee meeting, a two-hour closed roundtable with other non-verbal artists, and a visit to a grunt exhibition, with travel and access supports paid by the gallery. One deliverable is required — taking part in an interview, video or other response that is archived and shared publicly, due March 5, 2027 — and artists also meet grunt's program director, curator and/or exhibition manager for feedback on presenting their work to galleries. Two hard gates: applicants must live in the Greater Vancouver Regional District, and must have a silent or non-verbal art practice. The gallery is blunt that working in a quiet visual medium is not itself such a practice — the program is about navigating professional arts spaces without relying on speech, whether by choice, necessity or circumstance — and that it expects a long-standing practice (participants have typically had four years of focused work; hobbyists are told it is not a match). Priority goes to artists who self-identify as Deaf, deaf, Hard of Hearing, Non-Verbal or Neurodiverse, to Trans and Queer artists adapting to silence through voice-changing transitions, and to Indigenous artists from the Host Nations (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh). This is neither an exhibition nor a production residency and no maker or studio space is provided. No medium is named anywhere in the call, and grunt's own programme includes a lens-based photography residency, so photographers are not excluded — but the subject here is how you communicate, not what you shoot. Free to apply, by Google Form (a Google sign-in is required) or by emailing a plain-text or Microsoft Office application to aep@grunt.ca. Spring 2027 engagement runs February 2 – March 12, 2027, with a free ASL-interpreted info session on January 6, two days before the deadline. — Deadline: January 8, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000 CAD.

item.title: Jazz Fest Volunteer Photographer Program 2027 · New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation
