item.description: The New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation Archive selects photographers to document the 2027 New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival — the music, but also the food and art vendors, the cultural pavilion and the crowd — for permanent inclusion in the Foundation's historic collection. Selection is by a three-person blind jury of photographers scoring on artistic merit (60%) and experience photographing live cultural events or professional reliability (40%); no more than 150 applications are accepted. Photographers keep full ownership and copyright of their images, granting the Festival and Foundation permission to use them for non-commercial and educational purposes only, under a separate Terms of Agreement issued to those invited. Selected photographers are assigned one of the festival's two weekends (not both) and receive complimentary entry on assignment days, access to the Foundation hospitality lounge and free parking in designated lots, and may shoot the festival at leisure once the assignment is done. In return they must attend a compulsory photographers' meeting the day before the festival opens — that is where pit passes and tickets are issued — bring their own gear, deliver at least 18–24 photographs per act on their assigned stages with the selection left to the photographer, and be able to stand and walk long distances in heat, mud or dust. This is unpaid volunteer work: there is no fee to apply and no stipend — what comes back is credentialed access to a world-famous festival and a permanent place in a major cultural archive. Open internationally to student, amateur and professional photographers aged 18 or over; the application runs through CaFE and asks for six images, watermark-free. Two cautions about the Foundation's own page: the apply link in its How To Apply block points at a dead CaFE listing (ID 16128 — the live one is 18184, linked here under Submit via), and the same block dates the deadline November 13 while the page's own application-period header and CaFE both say November 14. Apply by November 13 to be safe. Festival dates are April 22–25 and April 29 – May 2, 2027. — Deadline: November 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Woodland Macro
item.description: Submit up to 5 images on the theme of woodland macro — close-up work made among trees, from fungi and bark to leaf detail and forest-floor life — for the 'One Thing This Month' reader competition (OP 334) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). The winner receives a Lowepro Fastpack BP 450 AW IV backpack (RRP £139). The challenge is pegged to the main technique feature in that issue of the magazine, and entrants are asked to type the competition theme into the corresponding field on the submission form. Entries need captions of up to 75 words covering where, why and how each image was taken, plus full technical details in the magazine's stated order (camera and lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture, tripod or handheld). Free to enter, uploaded in bulk through the magazine's Google Form, which requires a Google account because uploads run through Google Drive. The magazine publishes work taken outside in the landscape, wildlife, nature, adventure and travel genres — not fashion, wedding, field sports or interiors — and asks that images be made ethically and with sensitivity to environmental and conservation issues. Image manipulation is allowed but the magazine favours a gentle, sophisticated approach to editing. Entry is restricted to readers aged 18 or over, with one entry per person per competition, and the publisher's competition terms state that winners are notified by email within 30 days of the closing date and have 14 days to claim the prize. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Lowepro Fastpack BP 450 AW IV backpack (£139) + Publication.

item.title: Fridge Art Fair Miami 2026: Open Call for Artists
item.description: Fridge Art Fair returns to Miami Beach for Miami Art Week, December 1–6 2026, with “Gianni • Madonna • Coconuts”, which the fair describes as a citywide celebration of the Miami of the ’80s and ’90s, staged across three venues — the SoBe Visitor Center on Washington Ave, Uma House by Yurbban on James Ave and Habitat Hyett on Lincoln Road. Alongside the booth programme (booth fees start at $350–$500) the fair runs this open call, in which single works are submitted and assessed one at a time: “$35 for each work you submit … If your work is accepted, there is nothing more to pay. We take no commission on sales. You keep 100 percent of anything you sell.” The fair tells artists to “apply as many times as you like”, though the CaFE record itself caps an entrant at 20 applications, so 20 works is the real ceiling. Photography is named in the accepted-media list alongside painting, prints and drawing; work must be flat and wall-hung, no larger than 30 × 30 inches including the frame, projecting no more than 6 inches, under 35 pounds, wired and ready to hang. Sculpture and non-hanging work are considered case by case by email before applying. A jury reviews every work but no jurors are named, and there is no cash award — the return is the exhibition itself. One practical bar to weigh before entering: nothing can be shipped. Accepted artists, or a proxy, must drop off in person on November 29 or 30, attend their venue’s VIP opening night during fair week, and collect the work on December 7. Fridge does not insure artwork. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 per work. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist Spotlight 2026 · Associated Artists of Winston-Salem
item.description: Once a year the Associated Artists of Winston-Salem takes over the Main Gallery of the Milton Rhodes Center for the Arts — the Arts Council campus building in downtown Winston-Salem — for what it calls a “highly competitive juried exhibit” of recent bodies of work by a small number of its members. The ask is a portfolio rather than single images: artists may submit up to 20 pieces of which roughly 5–8 are chosen, and the prospectus wants “a common thread that reveals an artist’s commitment to a theme, concept, or aesthetics”. Selection is by a panel of three to five jurors described only as “acclaimed local artists”; no names are published. Awards are $250, $125 and $75 for first, second and third place. Photographs are explicitly eligible — “Hand-pulled prints, original digital prints, and photographs are all acceptable” — while printed reproductions of paintings or drawings are not. Entry requires AAWS membership, which is bought online and is not itself juried ($75 a year Associate, $20 for students), and anyone featured in an Artist Spotlight in the past three years is barred. Results are posted to ShowSubmit accounts by the end of October 23. Work is dropped off on November 2 and collected on January 30, 2027; the show runs November 6, 2026 – January 30, 2027, opening with a free public reception on the 6th. Sales split 70/30 in the artist’s favour. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: $50 for 6 works ($5 each additional, up to 20). Prize: $250 + $125 + $75 + Exhibition.

item.title: Multiplicity · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on multiplicity — seriality, collections, classification, typologies, diptychs, grids and other unified arrangements. The gallery's framing: when subjects are gathered, compared or arranged, ordinary forms become evidence of pattern, difference, accumulation and order; a collection becomes a portrait, a typology reveals variation. Images may be found or constructed, documentary or conceptual, black and white or colour, traditional or experimental. The juror is Ross Anderson. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (21 November – 12 December 2026), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived online. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future juried calls of the artist's choice), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames (mat openings up to 11 × 11, 10 × 15, 11.8 × 15 or 8 × 15 inches) and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 28 October 2026. The org's calls page prints the deadline with a typo ('Cct 18'); its SmarterEntry portal reads 'Closes Oct 18'. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: 48th Annual Whitewater Valley Art Competition · Indiana University East
item.description: The 48th edition of Indiana University East's annual juried competition, staged in the campus's Tom Thomas Gallery in Richmond, Indiana. All visual art mediums except video and sound are allowed, and the eligibility text names photographs alongside paintings, drawings, printmaking, digital artworks, ceramics, jewelry, sculpture, textiles, installation and mixed media. Artists must be 18 or older and reside in the United States; work must be original and cannot have been shown in a previous Whitewater Valley Art Competition, and no piece may exceed 60 inches in any direction. The $35 registration fee covers up to three entries (three different views of each piece may be uploaded; entering more than three separate works disqualifies the artist) and is paid on IU East's own payment link rather than through CaFÉ, which carries no fee. Images are submitted via CaFÉ by 14 October 2026 at 11:59pm; the juried rounds are pre-recorded and shared on Facebook Live on 23 October with breaks for live audience questions, so that is when accepted work becomes known. Accepted pieces must reach the gallery by 6 November (hand delivery 3–6 November), the artist's reception and awards presentation is on 14 November, and the exhibition runs 14 November 2026 – 9 April 2027 in the Tom Thomas Gallery and Meijer Artway. Awards come to over $2,000 in total award money — $1,000 for 1st Place plus an invitation to a 2027 solo exhibition, $500 for 2nd, $250 for 3rd and three Honorable Mentions of $100 each, alongside a Chancellor's Choice Purchase Award whose winning piece enters the Indiana University East Public Art Collection. Nothing in the awards block narrows the pool by medium. Work is insured while on exhibition (not in transit); the artist covers shipping both ways with a prepaid return label. Note the gallery's own web page still shows the 47th edition — the 48th cycle's details are published on the CaFÉ record. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 entries). Prize: $2,000+ in awards + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Birds! · Museum of Northern California Art
item.description: The Museum of Northern California Art (monca) in Chico seeks original artworks for its annual bird-themed exhibition, staged during Chico's 2027 Snow Goose Festival — 'work must showcase birds, of all kinds, in all media'. All media are accepted; the museum bars giclée prints of original non-photographic art and states 'No AI please'. Entry is limited to artists residing in Northern California, defined as 41 named counties from Alameda, Butte and Humboldt to Sacramento, San Francisco, Santa Clara, Sonoma and Yuba. The entry fee is $15 for the first work and $10 for each additional, up to eight, non-refundable whether or not work is accepted; the museum's exhibition committee of professional artists and collectors makes the selection, with results emailed on or before 19 November 2026. Accepted work is delivered 17–20 December 2026 or 7–10 January 2027 (the artist pays shipping both ways), must be wired for the museum's cable-and-hook rail (no sawtooth hangers), must not have been shown at monca before, and stays for the whole run: the show opens 14 January 2027 with a reception on 29 January and closes 7 March 2027, though the entry agreement text still carries an earlier 10 January 2027 closing date. There is no cash award; the return is a museum group show. Entries opened on CaFÉ on 22 September 2026 and the museum's own calls page had not yet posted this call at the time of listing. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $15 (first entry) + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Glassworks Magazine — Artwork Open Reading Period 2026
item.description: Free artwork submissions to Glassworks, the print literary magazine of Rowan University's Master of Arts in Writing programme in New Jersey. The magazine publishes still artwork — 'photography, paintings, collages, etc.' — bi-annually in its print issues, prefers to run several images by each artist selected, may add further images to its online galleries, and says it especially seeks to promote work by artists from marginalized communities. Submit five high-quality, print-ready images at 300 dpi or higher as JPG or PNG through Submittable. There is no submission fee: instead each genre carries a cap, and the artwork category closes as soon as 100 submissions are received or on 15 December 2026, whichever comes first, so early entry matters. One submission per genre per reading period; past contributors wait a full calendar year after publication before submitting again. AI-generated work is not accepted. Accepted contributors sign a contract granting exclusive first North American serial rights and first electronic publishing rights in English, with copyright reverting on publication; payment is one print copy of the issue, with a print-on-demand option for additional copies. The reading period opened 15 September 2026; the magazine's stated average response time is six months. Previously published work is not accepted, including work self-published online or on social media, and current Rowan University students, staff and faculty may not submit (alumni wait two years after graduating). — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print) + contributor copy.

item.title: Wildlife 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Printed photography exhibition on wildlife at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, 4 to 28 February 2027 - a theme the gallery says has not had its own dedicated exhibition there before. The brief asks for "the visual delight of wildlife and the stories that they tell", in natural habitats or the unusual places animals turn up, and it also invites work on wildlife's relationships with humans, "both positive and negative", from the exotic to the domestic and the rural to the urban. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee (a discount is offered to anyone selected for both of the gallery's February exhibitions, this and Golden Hour 2027), which covers printing at 16x12, 18x12 or 12x12 inches in gallery-owned frames. Selected participants have their work printed and hung in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the website and included in an exhibition catalogue, receive a digital certificate of participation, have photos and video of the installed work shared on the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for its Photographer of the Month. Submit 1 to 8 JPEGs at 300ppi and at least 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, in one batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address, stating which exhibition you are entering, your nationality or country of residence and any links. Deadline 9 October 2026; acceptance notification by 14 October (only selected photographers are notified) and payment due by 28 October. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Golden Hour 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Printed photography exhibition at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography, 4 to 28 February 2027, on the golden hour - the gallery's brief describes it as "the period of time in the day just after sunrise or just before sunset when an array of amazing colours can be captured", and asks for work that explores the world through the colour, light, shadow, texture and shape that light makes possible. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £50 participation fee (a discount is offered to anyone selected for both of the gallery's February exhibitions, this and Wildlife 2027), which covers printing at 16x12, 18x12 or 12x12 inches in gallery-owned frames. Selected participants have their work printed and hung in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the website and included in an exhibition catalogue, receive a digital certificate of participation, have photos and video of the installed work shared on the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for its Photographer of the Month. Submit 1 to 8 JPEGs at 300ppi and at least 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, in one batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address, stating which exhibition you are entering, your nationality or country of residence and any links. Deadline 9 October 2026; acceptance notification by 14 October (only selected photographers are notified) and payment due by 28 October. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Myth, Folk & Superstition: Surreal Fables · Der Greif
item.description: Open call from Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, for another edition of its Pulse online exhibitions, timed to launch on 31 October - "following on the heels of Halloween, just before Día de los Muertos and an upcoming Friday the 13th in November". The brief asks lens-based artists to explore modern folklore, cultural superstitions, myth-making and surrealism: from crossing paths with a black cat to honouring ancestors at vibrant altars, humans have always used stories, rituals and visual symbols to make sense of fate, luck and the unseen, and Der Greif wants photographic work that operates at the intersection of reality, fable and belief, whether staged cinematic storytelling, surreal dreamscapes or documentary studies of local legends, ancestral altars and talismanic objects. Selected artists are shown in an online exhibition in Der Greif's Pulse section, join an online roundtable critique with peers facilitated by Der Greif staff, and may be invited to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio, its route to artwork sales and commissions. Selection is on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community; the four staff jurors are named on the entry page. Submissions are one cohesive project not previously featured by Der Greif; the entry page and its upload form ask for at least 10 and up to 15 images, and the call's own conditions of participation agree, asking for “one project consisting of at least 10 images”. Der Greif's terms say the submission is free with an optional €10 donation and that artists who are unable or prefer not to contribute may request a free submission voucher by email, which the call page offers as a 50% or 100% discount code; the Picter listing's chip still reads 10 EUR. Open to photographers and videographers internationally, particularly emerging and mid-career artists, with no age or regional restriction. Deadline 14 October 2026 at 11:59pm CET; results are due on 30 October. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: Free (optional €10 donation). Prize: Online exhibition.
